threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think ‘Sainsbury’s’ is a grocery store, not a social hub. Locals know it’s just as much about the coffee and gossip.
Caught a guy on the N159 last night belting out Whitney Houston. Half the bus joined in, while the other half just stared, totally bemused.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid selling homemade lemonade at Sonnenallee, completely unbothered by the world, I knew I found my place.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can find spontaneous dance parties at abandoned U-Bahn stations. It’s like the city just lets loose, and you either join in or watch the magic unfold.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they casually drop the BART delays into conversation like it's just part of the evening weather report.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a mix of tourists and local street performers. One guy started beatboxing, and suddenly everyone was vibing. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the bars here close early, but more than a few stay open past 3 AM—just keep your ears open for the laughter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they stand still at intersections, staring up at each building like it’s their first trip to a fair.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to pay for the Dalston Junction toilet. Locals know it's a surprise entry fee that adds to the charm!
Caught a bloke on the 59 last night singing opera at the top of his lungs. Whole bus was in stitches, except a guy in the back who looked like he was plotting his escape.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh döner mingling with the sound of street musicians outside the U-Bahn station on a Saturday afternoon hit me. This is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand that doubles as an open-air gallery, showcasing local artists' work between the sausages.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their ability to seamlessly navigate BART delays and still show up at Dolores Park with takeout from La Taqueria, smiling.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, a guy tried to sell a cat on the 31 while belting out opera. The cat was unimpressed, but the whole bus stopped to hear him out.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think all siestas happen in the afternoon. But in Gràcia, many locals take a bite out before their evening plans, too.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the 8-minute wait for a tram after 10 PM; locals just know to switch to the night bus.
